BILINGUAL.EN: Example: Symbolic Differentiation
BILINGUAL.JA: 例：シンボリック微分

BILINGUAL.EN:
As an illustration of symbol manipulation and a further illustration of data abstraction, consider the design of a
procedure function
that performs symbolic differentiation of algebraic expressions. We would like the
procedure function
to take as arguments an algebraic expression and a variable and to return the derivative of the expression with respect to the variable. For example, if the arguments to the
procedure function
are $ax^2 + bx +c$ and$x$, the
procedure function
should return $2ax+b$. Symbolic differentiation is of special historical significance in
Lisp.
the programming language Lisp.The original version of this book used the programming language Scheme, a dialect of Lisp.
It was one of the motivating examples behind the development of a computer language for symbol manipulation. Furthermore, it marked the beginning of the line of research that led to the development of powerful systems for symbolic mathematical work, which are
currently being used by a growing number of applied mathematicians and physicists.
today routinely used by applied mathematicians and physicists.
BILINGUAL.JA: シンボル操作の例として、またデータ抽象のさらなる例として、代数式のシンボリック微分を行う手続き関数の設計を考えてみましょう。この手続き関数は、代数式と変数を引数として受け取り、その変数に関する式の導関数を返すようにしたいと思います。例えば、手続き関数への引数が $ax^2 + bx +c$ と$x$ であれば、手続き関数は $2ax+b$ を返すべきです。シンボリック微分は、Lispプログラミング言語 Lisp本書のオリジナル版はプログラミング言語 Scheme（Lisp の方言）を使用していました。において特に歴史的に重要な意味を持っています。シンボル操作のためのコンピュータ言語の開発を動機づけた例の一つでした。さらに、シンボリックな数学的作業のための強力なシステムの開発につながった研究の始まりを示すものであり、そのようなシステムは現在、ますます多くの応用数学者や物理学者に使われています。今日では応用数学者や物理学者に日常的に使われています。

BILINGUAL.EN: In developing the symbolic-differentiation program, we will follow the same strategy of data abstraction that we followed in developing the rational-number system of section. That is, we will first define a differentiation algorithm that operates on abstract objects such as sums, products, and variables without worrying about how these are to be represented. Only afterward will we address the representation problem.
BILINGUAL.JA: シンボリック微分プログラムの開発では、節の有理数システムの開発で従ったのと同じデータ抽象の戦略に従います。つまり、まず和、積、変数といった抽象オブジェクトに対して動作する微分アルゴリズムを定義し、それらがどのように表現されるかについては心配しません。表現の問題に取り組むのはその後です。

BILINGUAL.EN: The differentiation program with abstract data
BILINGUAL.JA: 抽象データを用いた微分プログラム

BILINGUAL.EN:
In order to
To
keep things simple, we will consider a very simple symbolic-differentiation program that handles expressions that are built up using only the operations of addition and multiplication with two arguments. Differentiation of any such expression can be carried out by applying the following differentiationrules for reduction rules:
BILINGUAL.JA: 話を単純にするために、2つの引数に対する加算と乗算の演算のみを使って構成される式を扱う、非常に単純なシンボリック微分プログラムを考えます。そのような式の微分は、次の differentiationrules for 簡約規則を適用することで実行できます。

TEXT.LATEX: \[ \begin{array}{rll} \dfrac{dc}{dx} & = & 0\quad \text{for $c$ a constant or a variable different from $x$} \\[12pt] \dfrac{dx}{dx} & = & 1 \\[12pt] \dfrac{d(u+v)}{dx} & = & \dfrac{du}{dx}+\dfrac{dv}{dx} \\[12pt] \dfrac{d(uv)}{dx} & = & u\left( \dfrac{dv}{dx}\right)+v\left( \dfrac{du}{dx}\right) \end{array} \]

BILINGUAL.EN: Observe that the latter two rules are recursive in nature. That is, to obtain the derivative of a sum we first find the derivatives of the terms and add them. Each of the terms may in turn be an expression that needs to be decomposed. Decomposing into smaller and smaller pieces will eventually produce pieces that are either constants or variables, whose derivatives will be either $0$ or $1$.
BILINGUAL.JA: 後の2つの規則は本質的に再帰的であることに注意してください。つまり、和の導関数を得るには、まず各項の導関数を求めてそれらを加えます。各項はさらに分解が必要な式である可能性があります。ますます小さい部分に分解していくと、最終的には定数か変数のいずれかの部分が得られ、その導関数は $0$ か $1$ のいずれかになります。

BILINGUAL.EN:
To embody these rules in a

If we had a means for representing algebraic expressions, we should be able to tell whether an expression is a sum, a product, a constant, or a variable. We should be able to extract the parts of an expression. For a sum, for example, we want to be able to extract the addend (first term) and the augend (second term). We should also be able to construct expressions from parts. Let us assume that we already have

SNIPPET.NAME: deriv
SNIPPET.SCHEME: (define (deriv exp var) (cond ((number? exp) 0) ((variable? exp) (if (same-variable? exp var) 1 0)) ((sum? exp) (make-sum (deriv (addend exp) var) (deriv (augend exp) var))) ((product? exp) (make-sum (make-product (multiplier exp) (deriv (multiplicand exp) var)) (make-product (deriv (multiplier exp) var) (multiplicand exp)))) (else (error "unknown expression type -- DERIV" exp))))
SNIPPET.JAVASCRIPT: function deriv(exp, variable) { return is_number(exp) ? 0 : is_variable(exp) ? is_same_variable(exp, variable) ? 1 : 0 : is_sum(exp) ? make_sum(deriv(addend(exp), variable), deriv(augend(exp), variable)) : is_product(exp) ? make_sum(make_product(multiplier(exp), deriv(multiplicand(exp), variable)), make_product(deriv(multiplier(exp), variable), multiplicand(exp))) : error(exp, "unknown expression type -- deriv"); }

BILINGUAL.EN:

the list (a * x + b).
list("a", "*", "x", "+", "b").
However, one especially straightforward choice is to use the same parenthesized prefix notation that Lisp uses for combinations; that is, to represent $ax+b$ as (+ (* a x) b). Then our
However, it will be more convenient if we reflect the mathematical structure of the expression in the JavaScript value representing it; that is, to represent $ax+b$ as list("+", list("*", "a", "x"), "b"). Placing a binary operator in front of its operands is called prefix notation prefix notation, in contrast with the infix notation introduced in section. With prefix notation, our
data representation for the differentiation problem is as follows:
